body: did this require a new test, or did the existing test already cover the branch?
Yes, a lot of tests needs to be updated. I'll redraft the PR until it's ready.
Stopping the method by returning early here breaks the existing behavior with customers who already init by themselves. I think it's better to let this run in this case.

A lot of tests fail because this mock file loads search-insights, which defines `window.AlgoliaAnalyticsObject`. I've deleted this reference, so tests would behave as if there were no insights on the global scope by default.

We had an error in the `__tests__/createInsightsMiddleware.ts` file on `insightsClient`:
```
Type 'Mock<void, [method: keyof InsightsMethodMap, options?: InitParams | undefined] | [method: keyof InsightsMethodMap, callback: (version: string) => void] | ... 12 more ... | [method: ...]>' is not assignable to type 'ProvidedInsightsClient'.
```
Not sure if there is a better way to fix this.
you can use the `castToJestMock` utility function we have that does the same

```suggestion
    if (!$$internal || insightsInitParams) {
```

this would require another test, but you can pass the init params to the insights option, so in that case we should still init.
Good catch, thanks Haroen, I added a test and updated the PR description.
This assumes the "default" middleware always uses a version that works without `init`, which might not be the case if Search Insights is already present but using an older v2 version, no?
good point, maybe it should be "shouldAddScript" as the condition instead?
@FabienMotte Would `isModernInsightsClient` use the `version`?
Yes, the function already exists: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/52f54bfb408c165f07184252f3737853b2c98a6c/packages/instantsearch.js/src/middlewares/createInsightsMiddleware.ts#L315

Yeah, so the only scenarios when `init` should be called are **when the user provides `insightsInitParams`** _or_ **when the Insights version doesn't support not calling `init`**.

But the fact that it's internal or not doesn't count here, am I correct?
I'd also clarify the condition, because `isModernInsightsClient` doesn't tell us what it actually supports.

Indeed, I removed the `$$internal` flag from the condition, thanks!

WDYT of `supportsOptionalInitMethod(insightsClient)`?
I liked modern more, as it is optional init + credentials through arguments. It's fine like this too of course
Either let's convey this with an explicit name, or use a comment, wdyt?
I guess technically "supportsOptionalInitMethod" covers both usages of the function, but I wonder if it should be "supportsCredentialsInPayload" or similar?

The function is called in both places, the first one being to check if the optional `init` method is supported and the other one is to check if the credentials are supported as extra params.

So maybe we should keep a generic function name like `isModernInsightsClient()` that encapsulates both behavior and add comments at both places of use, WDYT?
